title: The hard case, named first
question: Who asks a sceptic to pay for a promise, in under a hundred words, and gets believed? (Q13, the voice round)
serves: North star 1 (a distinctive, human voice) and 4 (investing knowledge, applied); Commandments III-V; Investment Strategy and Portfolio Analysis (a rule that holds across market outcomes), Creativity & Presentation
essence: We read people who sell promises to doubters, in their own words: annuity sellers, auction houses and mountain guides, and every one of the 37 lines we re-checked was real.

What they share is naming the bad case before the buyer can and saying exactly where it sits; the one clause worth taking into the IPS is that the gift's promised half moves into Treasuries on naming day 'even in a week when stocks are rising'.

Felix found the bigger point: the mountain story argues for buying the floor early, and shows the 2031 lock is still a step someone has to take on the day, so the Lab now tests what a late or skipped lock costs.
decided: KEEP narrowly (Felix, after checking): slip S-10's IPS move is one clause, 'even in a week when stocks are rising'; no mountain, Hall or Loewenstein in the IPS or pitch
The turnaround argues for the 2028 floor more than the 2031 lock (Amara conceded, Felix agreed): the lock is an instruction doing an asset's work, the plan's softest place

CORD (Felix): V47 holds all three paragraphs (P6 Jun's, P7 Amara's, P8 Kai's), so there is no live-version question; Kai's four numbers are V47's own, sourced to Archive A26, which Felix re-opened and which matches

None of the three rewrites fixes the Window's two near-breaches (Kai's prints NB2 instead); the fixes stay the Window's: S1's $85,000 v $135,000 costs no words, and the NB1 bridge is +14 strict, not +11
Hall goes to the Final Report only as the failure case, in a sentence that ends with his rule failing; Mountain Trip's published pace test parked for the Final Report

Dropped: mortality credits (no pool, no life condition in Laura's cheques); Phillips' disclaiming voice; the 'deposit = acceptance' row (it maps backwards); the hot-cold empathy gap as used (named, not applied; the Ulysses contract, bank #81, already holds the idea)
seeds: Lock-timing test: the lock a month or a quarter late, and skipped where stocks rose most before naming; top reached in S0, S1, S6 (Genius Lab)
Order test: if the promised half moves before she names the range, does any V47 number change? If not, the lock is a precondition and Kai's 'who holds the watch?' is answered by design (Genius Lab)
A condition report on our own plan for the Final Report's risk section: each flaw with its address (which year, which paths), then one 'However' (Writing Room, after 7 Nov)
